newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Cathay Pacific says may seek cash from Rolls.
newsitem.headline: HK's Cathay Pacific says may seek cash from Rolls.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Thursday it might ask Rolls-Royce Plc for compensation after the Hong Kong carrier grounded its fleet of Airbus A330-300 aircraft due to problems with Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.
"That is something that we will have to seriously consider," Cathay Pacific chairman Peter Sutch told government radio.
"Cathay will of course have lost some money," he said. "One cannot deny that. It's too early to put an accurate figure on it."

Cathay Pacific cancelled 12 flights on Thursday -- four to Hong Kong and eight from Hong Kong -- but the airline said it was making every effort to find "alternative ways to get passengers to their destination".
"Despite the temporary suspension of our A330-300 services, Cathay Pacific will be operating 90 percent of its flights today," it said in a statement.
The airline said it was also operating charter flights from Air Canada, Singapore Airlines and Air Mauritius to cover for the cancellations resulting from the groundings.
Cathay Pacific and its 25.5 percent owned Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) grounded their twin-engined A330-300 aircraft on Saturday, disrupting normal flight services.
Cathay operates 11 A330-300 and Dragonair has four.
The groundings followed the failure last week of a Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engine on a Dragonair flight, forcing the aircraft to make a single-engine landing in the Philippines.
It was the fifth time since November a Cathay Pacific or Dragonair A330-300 had made a single-engine landing.
The carrier has predicted its A330-300s will be flying again by mid-June.
Rolls-Royce says it has found a solution to the problem, which it said stemmed from the gearbox lubrication system. The gearboxes are supplied by France's Hispano Suiza, it says.
Rolls-Royce declined on Tuesday to comment on the subject of compensation to Cathay and Dragonair.
